## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Surendranath Dasgupta refers to "Apadana 153" in passing, citing the phrase *anāhāro nibbāyettha* in his discussion of early Buddhist metaphors that liken *nibbāna* to a fire dying down through lack of fuel rather than one violently extinguished [Dasgupta 1941].

**Sources**

- [Dasgupta 1941] Surendranath Dasgupta, Philosophical Essays (1941) — citation of Apadana 153 regarding the fire metaphor for nibbāna
